Market Capitalization
Adjustment to Shares Outstanding

Stock splits - Changes nothing fundamentally – price changes by the split ratio in addition to the shares – no change in market capitalization
Types of stock splits
Forward Stock split –examples 2:1 or 3:1
A corporate action whereby for every share held before the split, each stockholder will have two or three shares, respectively, after the split.
Reverse stock split – opposite of a forward stock split. The number of shares outstanding is reduced and the price of the stock increases by the ratio of the split
Why do a stock split transaction?
Lower absolute stock price allows individuals to buy more full shares vs partial shares
Better overall liquidity in the market
Raise share price above a minimum regulator threshold for delisting

What is a Fair Market Capitalization for a company's stock?

Valuation Methodologies:  Absolute vs Relative
Absolute Valuation – Discounted Cash Flow Valuation 5 steps\n

Estimate long term future cashflows for a firm (eternity???)
Determine Discount Rate to use -  WACC – weighted average cost of capital
Determine cost of debt
Determine cost of equity
Determine weighted average
Take the estimated future cash flows/divide by WACC to get the value of the future earnings today
Value of cashflows diminish the further out you go
Higher WACC erodes the value of future cashflows – inherently more risk and volatility in future cash flows
Deduct the firm’s indebtedness and add in the firm’s cash to derive the est. market capitalization
Divide estimated market cap by the number of share to get a fair share price from the valuation
Cost of equity = CAPM – capital asset pricing model – uses stock beta to account for the riskiness of stocks\n

Relative Valuation

Relative Valuation – compared to other companies or the market to determine relative value – determines if a company is over valued, under valued or fairly valued. It does not determine the exact fair market price of the stock.
Pros – easier to understand – comparison shopping. Simple to calculate, does not demand long term forecasts,
Cons – directional, hard to find truly comparable companies, presupposes that the company you are comparing it to is fairly valued too

Valuation Methodology Summary

Absolute Valuation Summary
Absolute valuation involves the discount of future cash flows
Future profits in the long term are worth less than profits in the short term
Good financial models balance simplicity with insight
The concept of absolute valuation is theoretically perfect
The outputs from absolute valuations are usually precisely wrong
Relative Value Summary
Relative Valuation is the quick and easy comparison of one valuation to another
The risk of relative valuation is being led astray by unrealistic reference points
Earnings and multiples are used to estimate fair share prices
Fast growing companies warrant higher multiples and vice versa
The state of the economy is a key driver of relative valuation
Equity Module & Terminal Function Review

Index movements are driven by movements in member stocks
The volatility of earnings leads to volatility of share prices
Uncovering industry drives is key to estimate earnings
Absolute valuation is in theory perfect but has practical limitations
Relative valuation is easier but sensitive to earnings growth - & the right peers
Roller coaster – Economy. Earnings, Stock Markets – future is unknowable
